subject.title: Prompt-cache prefix churn on OpenAI models: per-turn dynamic injections (message tool hint + volatile system-prompt section) defeat automatic prefix caching

question: Should OpenClaw make message-tool schema and delivery guidance byte-stable for OpenAI/Codex cache paths, and where should per-turn `message_tool_only` guidance live?
rationale: The remaining fix is not a purely mechanical cleanup because it changes where user-visible delivery instructions are carried while preserving message-tool-only correctness.

options.title: Stabilize Tool Schema
options.body: Keep the message tool schema identical across delivery modes and place the per-turn visible-reply instruction in late-bound turn content or another non-cache-prefix surface.

options.title: Preserve Current Schema Split
options.body: Accept the cache churn as the cost of making delivery guidance part of the tool contract for message-tool-only runs.

options.title: Defer For Live Proof
options.body: Wait for fresh OpenAI/Codex telemetry from current main before choosing the implementation boundary.

recommendation.title: Stabilize Tool Schema
recommendation.body: Keep the message tool schema identical across delivery modes and place the per-turn visible-reply instruction in late-bound turn content or another non-cache-prefix surface.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest recent history signal across the affected runtime and provider files, though the original ownership trail is obscured.
